questions.prompt: Which is the right bring-up order for a new robot board?
options: Motors, then sensors, then comms, then power, because motors show problems fastest and then retest everything.
Power, reset and clock, comms, sensors, actuators at low power, then the closed loop.
Closed loop first, then comms, then sensors, then power, so the control code is proven early.
Sensors, then power, then actuators, then comms, in whatever order the parts arrive and then retest everything.
questions.explanation: A fault upstream makes everything downstream look broken, so test from the source: power first, motors and the loop last, with the wheels off the ground.

questions.prompt: Four NiMH cells (4.8 V open circuit, 0.4 ohm total series resistance) supply a motor that draws 2 A at start. What is the voltage in volts during the start?
An ESP32 board resets only when the motor starts and the boot log says BROWNOUT_RST. What is the most likely cause?
options: The serial baud rate is wrong and then retest everything before touching anything else.
A floating input on the button pin and then retest everything.
Two I2C devices share one address and then retest everything.
The supply voltage sags under the motor's start current.
questions.explanation: BROWNOUT_RST means the supply dipped below the detector level. Resets that line up with motor start point to sag from inrush current (V = Voc - I*R).

questions.prompt: I2C fast mode: rise time limit 300 ns, bus capacitance 100 pF. Maximum pull-up resistance Rp,max = tr / (0.8473 * Cb) in ohms, precision 5.
A button input with nothing attached reads random 0 and 1. What fixes it?
options: Enable INPUT_PULLUP, or add an external 10 k pull-up or pull-down.
Raise the baud rate and then retest everything before touching anything else.
Add a delay(100) in loop() and then retest everything before touching anything else.
Power the board from a bigger battery and then retest everything before touching anything else.
questions.explanation: A floating input picks up noise. A pull-up or pull-down gives it a defined level.
questions.skillLabel: Logic levels, pull-ups and floating inputs

questions.prompt: An MPU-6050 and a DS1307 are on one I2C bus and both answer at 0x68. Which fix works?
options: Lower the baud rate of the serial port and then retest everything.
Add a second 10 k pull-up to SDA and then retest everything.
Wire the MPU-6050 AD0 pin high so it moves to 0x69.
Swap the SDA and SCL wires and then retest everything before touching anything else.
questions.explanation: The MPU-6050 has an address pin: AD0 high gives 0x69. The DS1307 address is fixed, so move the other device, use a multiplexer or a second bus.

questions.prompt: Write a minimal test plan for a new wheel module before the wheel touches the ground: at least five tests in order, each with a measurable pass criterion.
rubric: Orders the tests power first (continuity, idle current, rails), then reset reason, comms, sensors, and only then the motor at low duty with the wheel in the air.
Gives measurable pass criteria such as rails within 5 %, one boot banner, scan matches the map, count direction and counts per revolution, current under a limit.
Includes a safety test (timeout stops the output) and says what to record: firmware version, pin map and measurements.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
